reading-review/paper-vs-screen.reason: downgraded A→B: tie-break 4 applies. Delgado et al. 2018 report I² = 72.24 for between-participant studies and I² = 89.88 for within-participant studies, which had no moderator analysis (10.1016/j.edurev.2018.09.003). Their prediction intervals span zero (−.56 to .14, and −.90 to .47), and they note "clearly unexplained variance". The newest meta-analysis, by the same group, finds g = −0.11 for handheld devices, with I² = 94.39 (Salmerón et al. 2024; 10.1037/edu0000830). It also reports that tablet studies varying the time frame "resulted in null effects", so the "under time limits" clause is unsettled too.

reading-review/automation-bias.reason: downgraded B→C: the B fits only the claim's first sentence. The second sentence, that forcing interventions reduce overreliance, rests on one experiment (Buçinca et al. 2021, N = 199; 10.1145/3449287). Against it, automation bias "cannot be prevented by training or instructions" (Parasuraman & Manzey 2010; 10.1177/0018720810376055), and Mosier et al.'s accountability manipulation had no effect. That is few studies with mixed results.
